fields.description:
## Context / Problem
The deployed MCP server mints op-cert signatures it can never verify. Every attestation it
produces — the plan-review cert at claim and the completion-verifier cert at close — is
permanently uncertifiable on the same box, so `claim` through the deployed server is refused
for every ticket.

Observed 2026-08-27 against the LIVE MCP server (`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`),
signing and then immediately verifying on the same server:

```
sign_manifest {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered", "manifest": ["probe: ..."]}
  -> {"algorithm": "sshsig", "key_id": "9f1c8e42-...", "envelope": "{...}"}   # SUCCEEDS

verify_signature {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered"}
  -> {"verified": false, "verdict": "foreign_key",
      "reason": "this environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature"}
```

`claim_gate_check` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py:113-133`) reads a non-`verified`
result as "no certified plan-review attestation" and denies the claim. That is the P1.

## Mechanism — sign and verify resolve the key from two DIFFERENT places
This is a path mismatch, not a missing file. The signing and verifying halves do not share a
key-resolution chain.

SIGN side — `ensure_opcert_key` (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:155-206`) resolves, in order:
the context-local startup binding's process-owned key copy; else `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`; else
the `<tracker>/.opcert-key` genesis. The deployed server takes the FIRST branch:
`compose_startup_opcert_binding` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:717-746`) composes a signer from
`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` + `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` (`/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key`), and
`run_mcp` binds it around the serving loop (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:325-329`), so every tool
call signs under a process-owned copy of the MOUNTED key.

VERIFY side — `_opcert_own_public_key` (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:238-258`) consults NEITHER
the binding NOR `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`. It reads `<tracker>/.opcert-key.pub`, and its
self-healing branch re-derives that `.pub` only from `<tracker>/.opcert-key`. On this box the
tracker holds NEITHER file (verified in-container: only `.env-id` and `.ensure-applied`), so the
self-heal cannot fire and the function returns `None`. `verify_opcert_record`
(`:528-535`) then answers `foreign_key`.

The tracker re-clone (`7be0edb7132d`) is context, not the cause: even with a tracker-local
keypair present, it would be a DIFFERENT keypair from the mounted signing key, so verification
would still fail (as `mismatch` rather than `foreign_key`). Regenerating tracker-local key
material is therefore NOT a fix.

`REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` is likewise not a fix: it is read only by the SIGN-side
`ensure_opcert_key`, which the bound server does not even reach, and the verify-side reader
never consults it.

## Impact
rebar mints exactly two op-cert kinds (ADR 0049). On this server both are
signed-but-uncertifiable: the claim gate refuses every ticket, and a close records a
`completion_signature` that `verify_signature` cannot certify. A project that later enables
`verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since` would find every attestation this
server produced rejected. Signing succeeds while verification is structurally impossible, so
nothing surfaces the problem when the certificate is minted.

## Reproduction
1. Against the deployed MCP server, call `sign_manifest` on any ticket with a one-item manifest.
2. Observe it succeeds and returns an `sshsig` envelope.
3. Call `verify_signature` on the same ticket.
4. Observe `verdict: "foreign_key"`, reason "this environment has no op-cert public key".

## Fix
Make the verify side resolve the public half from the SAME ordered chain the sign side resolves
the private half (binding, then `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`, then tracker genesis), deriving the
public line in-process from the resolved private key with `ssh-keygen -y`. Deriving — rather
than shipping a second secret — is required because the deployment key is bind-mounted
READ-ONLY, so no `.pub` cache can be written beside it; the derived text, not a file, is the
authority. No new secret, mount, or deploy change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: On the deployed MCP server, a `sign_manifest` immediately followed by
  `verify_signature` on the same ticket returns `verdict: "certified"`, `verified: true`.
- [ ] AC2: `_opcert_own_public_key`'s successor resolves the public key from the same ordered
  chain as `ensure_opcert_key` — bound startup signer, then `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`, then
  `<tracker>/.opcert-key` — deriving the public line in-process from the resolved private key.
  The deployment ships no additional key material.
- [ ] AC3: Deriving the public line never requires writing beside the private key: a key whose
  directory is read-only (the bind-mounted secret) still certifies.
- [ ] AC4: The unbound tracker-genesis path is unchanged, including its `.pub` cache write, and
  verification still never creates a private key.
- [ ] AC5 (DEFERRED, follow-up): `sign_manifest` emits an explicit WARNING — it does not refuse,
  so no existing sign flow breaks — when the environment cannot resolve a public counterpart for
  the key it just signed under.
- [ ] AC6 (DEFERRED, follow-up): a deploy/startup health check fails when the signing key has no
  usable public counterpart, so this cannot regress silently.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] DD1: AC2, AC3 and AC4 covered by a regression test that is RED before the fix and GREEN
  after it — `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_own_pub_resolution_d26a.py`.
- [ ] DD2: AC1 demonstrated against the deployed MCP server after the change is deployed.
